HAUNTLIGHT / A little light. A different world.
Source code ↓
Double-tap anywhere for controls

From iPad to after dark.

  1. Connect the projector. For wireless mirroring, connect an Apple TV to the Epson’s HDMI input, then choose it from iPad Control Center → Screen Mirroring. A Lightning Digital AV Adapter with HDMI is the wired option. The 980W is not a native AirPlay receiver.
  2. Add Hauntlight to your Home Screen. Open in Safari, sign in if prompted, then Share → Add to Home Screen. Launch the icon for a cleaner full-screen experience. Use landscape orientation and keep the iPad powered.
  3. Keep it awake. Set Settings → Display & Brightness → Auto-Lock → Never for the show, then restore your preference afterward. Automatic wake lock is unreliable in older iPad Home Screen apps.
  4. Map the light. Choose a layout, press Align, and drag the corners against your actual objects. Grid helps you focus. Double-tap for controls; return to the editor when aligned. Use Align and Project in the same orientation and full-screen state.
  5. Press Project. The editor disappears. Double-tap to reveal controls; use Blackout to temporarily blank the image. Black pixels cannot eliminate projector light leakage.

The Epson’s native image is 1280 × 800. iPad mirroring can add black bars; choose a projector aspect mode that preserves the image and calibrate after connecting. This app mirrors one view; it cannot keep private controls on the iPad while sending a separate view to the projector.

Best outdoors after dark on light, matte surfaces. Keep the projector dry. Start with 1–3 surfaces on iPad 5; six is the maximum, not a performance guarantee. No flashing/strobe presets are included.

Layouts stay in this browser. Export JSON for backup or transfer. The app uses a vendored MIT-licensed perspective-transform core. Physical iPad/projector testing is still required.
